<entry id="U00973">
<head-word>שִׁינּוּי</head-word>
<head-word>שִׁנּ'</head-word>
<pos> m.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (שָׁנָה) 
<italic>change.</italic></definition>
<notes> Gen. R. s. 44 ש' השם change of name; ש' מקום change of residence. Sabb. 114
<sup>a</sup> top ש' בגדים change of dress (for the Sabbath, for prayer &c.). Keth. 110
<sup>b</sup>, a. e. ש' וסת, v. וֶסֶת; a. fr.—Esp. (law) 
<italic>change of form</italic> (and 
<italic>name</italic>) 
<italic>effected on an illegitimately obtained object</italic>, by which the present possessor is privileged to retain the object and pay its value. B. Kam. 65
<sup>b</sup> נעשה ש' בידו וקנאו the change (from calf to ox) happened while the animal was in his possession, and he has obtained ownership. Ib. וניקנינהו בש' השם may he not have obtained the ownership of it through the change of name? Ib. ש' במקומו עומד (not עומדת) the change stands in its (the original’s) place, i.e. the change of form or name of an object does not affect its legal status; ib. 93
<sup>b</sup>; ib. 68
<sup>a</sup> ש' במקומה עומד. Ib. 66
<sup>b</sup> ש' מעשה (= ש' ע"י מעשה) a change brought about by human action. Ib. 68
<sup>a</sup>, a. fr. ש' רשות change of possession (by transfer of the object to a third person). Ib. 93
<sup>b</sup> ש' דרבנן a change which gives the right of ownership by rabbinical ordinance, i.e. ש' החוזר לברייתו (ib. 67
<sup>a</sup>) a change (of name) which can be undone by restoring the object to its original condition; ש' דאורייתא a change which gives the right of ownership by Biblical law, i.e. a change which cannot be undone; a. fr.—Men. 43
<sup>a</sup> וסימנך ש' שקר ש' אמת and the mnemonical word (to remember which change proves the color to be genuine (תכלת), and which proves it to be adulterated) is ‘a false change’ (one who changes his word for evil is a bad man), ‘a true change’ (one who changes his word to do better than he has promised).—Sifra Vayikra, Ḥob., ch. XIX, Par. 11; Meïl. 18
<sup>a</sup>, v. שִׁיקּוּר I.—
<plural-form>Pl. שִׁינּוּיִים, שִׁינּוּיִין</plural-form>. B. Kam. 65
<sup>b</sup> (ref. to גם, Deut. XXIII, 19) לרבות שִׁינּוּיֵיהֶם this serves to include in the prohibition these objects even when they have been changed in form; Tem. 30
<sup>b</sup>; a. e.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<sup>b</sup> כל שִׁיעוּרֵי שבת all legal minimum sizes for eatables carried abroad on the Sabbath; a. fr.—Ib. 35
<sup>b</sup> נתת דבריך לש' thy rule would vary according to circumstances, and would not be alike for all; Meg. 18
<sup>b</sup>; a. fr.—Y. B. Bath. V, end, 15

<sup>b</sup> (Ms. M. לשֵׁיד).—כלי ש' musical instruments (used in the Temple during the offering of sacrifices). Taan. IV (III), 3; a. e.—
<plural-form>Pl. שִׁירִים, שִׁירִין</plural-form>. Cant. R. to I, 1 דוד אמר ש' ושלמה אמר ש' David composed songs, and so did Solomon. Ib. end (expl. שיר השירים) המעולה שבש'; המסולסל שבש', v. סִלְסֵל. <italic>Song of Songs</italic> (

<senses>
<sense>
<definition> v. 
<xref rid="U01055">שִׁיר II</xref>)

<sup>a</sup> עיקר ש' בפה וכלי וכ' the essential in the Temple music is (the song) with the mouth, and the musical instruments are for accompaniment (v. בְּסַם); (anoth. opin.) עיקר ש' בכלי instrumental music is the essential &c.; Succ. 50
<sup>b</sup>; a. e.—Y. Meg. III, 74
<sup>b</sup> bot. שִׁירַת הבאר the song of the well (Num. XXI, 17 sq.); ש' הים the song of the sea (Ex. XV, 1—18); ש' הלוים the song of the Levites (for the additional sacrifice of the Sabbath, Deut. XXXII, 1–43); Treat. Sof’rim ch. XII. R. Hash. 30

<plural-form>Pl. שִׁירוֹת</plural-form>. Y. Meg. l. c. כל הש' טעונות וכ' all poetic passages of the Pentateuch (when read at public service) require special benedictions before and after. Ex. <entry id="U01145">

<pos> f.</pos>

<sense>
<definition> (שָׁכַב) </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>lying down, lying position</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ber. 11
<sup>a</sup> (ref. to Deut. VI, 7) בשעת ש' ש' ממש וכ' at the time of lying down, (and) literally in a reclining position, and at the time of rising, (and) literally in an erect position (must the Sh’mʿa be recited, v. קִימָה a correct quot. acc.). Ib. 4
<sup>b</sup> מקיש ש' לקימה וכ' the text (Deut. l. c.) puts lying down parallel to rising, as at rising (in the morning) the reading of the Sh’mʿa precedes the prayer (תְּפִלָּה), אף ש' וכ' so at lying down (in the evening) the reading of the Sh’mʿa precedes &c. Ib. מאי קימה … אף ש' נמי סמוך למיטתו as in the morning the Sh’mʿa is read near the bed (immediately after rising), so in the evening the Sh’mʿa is read near the bed (before going to bed). Y. ib. I, 3
<sup>c</sup> מפני שכתוב בה ש' וקימה because lying down and rising are mentioned therein (in the chapter of Balaam, Num. XXIII, 24; XXIV, 9). Y. Gitt. III, 44
<sup>d</sup> top; Tosef. Kel. B. Mets. I, 14 אחת לש' וכ' one mattress to lie on, and another &c.; a. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>lying with, carnal connection</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Snh. 54
<sup>b</sup> (ref. to Lev. XVIII, 2</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>3)</number>
<definition> לא תתן שְׁכָבְתְּךָ … שְׁכִיבָתְךָ thou shalt not give thy 
<italic>sh’khobeth</italic> means, thou shalt not allow thy lying with (any connection, either active or passive); Yalk. Ex. 348; Yalk. Lev. 599.</definition>
<notes> Snh. l. c. לדברי … שכבתך ושכיבתך חדא היא according to R. ʿAk. he is guilty of one act only, for thy 
<italic>sh’khobeth</italic> and thy 
<italic>sh’khibah</italic> are the same.</notes></sense></senses></entry>
